cards.title: Core idea
cards.body: Caching stores a copy of frequently read data in a faster layer so most reads skip the database or origin. It works because reads vastly outnumber writes and access is skewed: a few keys get most reads. Every cache trades some staleness for speed.

cards.title: How it works
cards.body: The common pattern is cache-aside: check the cache; on a miss read the database and fill the cache; on a write update the database and delete the key. Delete instead of update because concurrent writers can leave a permanently wrong value. Eviction frees memory; invalidation removes changed data.

questions.a: no-cache may be stored but must be revalidated before use; no-store must never be stored.

questions.q: After a Redis restart the database hits 100 percent CPU. Why?
questions.a: It was sized for cache-hit traffic; a cold cache sends every read to it. Use stampede protection, warm-up and headroom.

questions.q: A user saw another user's account page. What happened?
questions.a: A shared cache stored a personalized response, missing private or no-store, or the key lacked the user. Purge and fix headers.
